results.title: Why Open Models Get Faster Weeks After Launch
results.author: Niklas
highlights:
Published on 2026.10.31 by Niklas

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next was released on August 26, 2026. The same day, SGLang announced day-0 support, built with the Qwen, NVIDIA and AMD teams, and shipped a dedicated container image. vLLM served the model from its own dedicated image while the architecture-support work was still being merged. llama.cpp, the engine most people use to run models on their own hardware, picked up initial support in version 0.4.0 with a release note saying optimization improvements were still pending.

...

For a hosted API, the cost of serving a token is roughly the cost of a GPU hour divided by the tokens that GPU produces in that hour. When engine work raises throughput, the cost per token falls even though the hardware bill does not change. If a node costs the same per hour and serves 1.5 times as many tokens, the cost per token drops by about a third.

Three of the improvements above act on that ratio directly:

- Cache memory savings (like the host-memory offload) let each GPU hold more concurrent requests
- Lower-precision weights move fewer bytes per token
- Fused kernels waste fewer cycles on overhead

Speculative decoding mostly improves latency for each individual request, and its effect on cost depends on load. It helps most when the GPU would otherwise be underused, which is typical at low batch sizes, and helps less when the hardware is already busy with large batches.

Providers do not all pass savings through at the same pace, and some never reprice. But the underlying cost curve moves, and competitive pressure among providers of an open model tends to pull prices toward it.

Granite-4.2-8B Pricing Guide: Provider Comparison

# Granite-4.2-8B Pricing Guide: Provider Comparison

Published on 2026.10.18 by DeepInfra

Granite-4.2-8b is a practical pick for anyone shopping for a small open-weight reasoning model. It costs $0.06 per million input tokens and $0.25 per million output tokens. It also scores 11 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index among small (4B to 40B) open-weight models.

Its input price sits below the $0.12 median for comparable models, and its output price matches the $0.25 median. You can reach it directly or through routed access across multiple providers.

Granite-4.2-8b is an 8-billion-parameter reasoning model from IBM’s Granite family, released in late August 2026 and post-trained from Granite-4.1-8B-Base. It is a decoder-only dense transformer with text-in, text-out support, an Apache 2.0 license, and public weights on Hugging Face.

...

## Granite-4.2-8b Executive Summary

Granite-4.2-8b is priced for cost-conscious production use. It costs $0.06/M input, $0.25/M output, and $0.015/M cached tokens on DeepInfra. OpenRouter lists the same rates on its DeepInfra route, and CoreWeave offers $0.10/M input, $0.15/M output, and $0.05/M cached tokens.

It suits teams that want an Apache 2.0 reasoning model with long context, tool calling, and flexible deployment. DeepInfra is the strongest choice for low-cost direct access, while CoreWeave and OpenRouter are the main alternatives.

# GLM-5.3 Is Now Available on DeepInfra

Published on 2026.10.03 by DeepInfra

GLM-5.3 shares its base model with GLM-5.2, so every performance gain comes from post-training. Z.ai scaled the reinforcement learning stack it already had and released the result on August 14, 2026. GLM-5.3 is a reasoning model built for complex software engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks. On Z.ai’s internal Code Bench, it improves 50% over GLM-5.2, and Z.ai reports it uses fewer output tokens to get there.

...

GLM-5.3 is now available on DeepInfra.

...

## Getting Started on DeepInfra

GLM-5.3 is available now on DeepInfra under the model identifier zai-org/GLM-5.3. A 38% promotional discount is currently active. Pricing is $0.563 per 1M input tokens, $2.50 per 1M output tokens, and $0.125 per 1M cached input tokens. List price without the promotion is $0.90, $4.00, and $0.20, so budget against list price for anything beyond the promotional window.

The Flex tier takes a further 20% off, bringing current rates to $0.45, $2.00, and $0.10. It applies the same reduction to input, output, and cache, and it stacks with the promotion. GLM-5.3 supports Flex and does not list a Priority tier. The model runs at fp4 quantization, supports the full 1,048,576-token context window, and has function calling and JSON output enabled out of the box.

...

DeepInfra offers an OpenAI-compatible API, so swapping your base URL and API key works with existing tooling. Pricing is usage-based with no minimums. The platform operates a zero-retention policy and holds SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certifications.
